decision.reason: The selected Arabic does not explicitly settle the attribution in English. Ibn Hajar treats the introduction as Abu Hurayrah’s words; al-Ayni offers a Prophetic attribution through an unexpressed reporting link. The two English comparisons take different approaches. Preserve the full eight Arabic paragraphs, six verse lines and closing corroborating routes as evidence, without selecting a translated speaker.

classicalCommentary.locator: Night Prayer, the Abu Hurayrah / Ibn Rawahah poem; discussion of إن أخا لكم and the closing Zubaydi route
classicalCommentary.observation: Fath al-Bari identifies Abu Hurayrah as the speaker and disputes Ibn Battal’s attribution. Umdat al-Qari, in its discussion of the closing route, suggests that Abu Hurayrah omitted the reporting link to the Prophet. This is a material attribution decision, not permission to discard the poem or closing chain.
